CME Group "Event Contracts" on futures — daily-expiring, cash-settled, European-style binary options on futures, CME/CBOT/NYMEX/COMEX Rulebook Chapter 23. Eleven Globex roots, all confirmed still listed in CME's July 2026 event-contract specification PDF:

ECES  (Event Contracts on E-mini S&P 500 futures, CME 23A, underlying ES)
ECNQ  (E-mini Nasdaq-100, CME 23B, underlying NQ)
ECRTY (E-mini Russell 2000, CME 23C, underlying RTY; clearing code truncates to ECRT — CME's own docs also mis-spell it "ERTY")
ECYM  (E-mini Dow, CBOT 23A, underlying YM)
EC6E  (Euro/U.S. Dollar FX, CME 23D, underlying 6E)
ECCL  (Light Sweet Crude Oil, NYMEX 23D, underlying CL)
ECNG  (Henry Hub Natural Gas, NYMEX 23E, underlying NG)
ECGC  (Gold, COMEX 23A, underlying GC)
ECSI  (Silver, COMEX 23B, underlying SI)
ECHG  (Copper, COMEX 23C, underlying HG)
ECBTC (Bitcoin Futures, CME chapter 23, underlying BTC — added later, see revisions)

SCOPE WARNING for the crate: CME now sells several *different* product families under the "event contract"/"Prediction Markets" umbrella, and they do NOT share this profile. Do not fold these in:
  - Swap-based economic/crypto event contracts (ECCPI, ECGDP, ECNFP, ECUNE, ECPCE, ECFD; CCB10/CCB11/CCB13/CCB15/CCB16 hourly Bitcoin/Ether) — CME Rulebook Chapter 22, listed per SER-9586RR, with a wholly different grid ("a one (1) minute trading halt each day from 5:00 P.M. ET to 5:01 P.M. ET" plus "the CME Globex maintenance period of 3:00 A.M. ET - 5:00 A.M. ET on Saturday and Tuesday").
  - Hourly Event Contracts on futures (SER-9624, Oct 15 2025): "CME Globex: Sunday 6:00 p.m. - Friday 5:00 p.m. ET with a daily maintenance period from 5:00 p.m. - 6:00 p.m. ET".
  - Sports/political event contracts (FG*/FS*/NG* team codes, CME FSPI).

result.reuse_verdict:
DIRECT ANSWER TO THE KEY QUESTION: Yes, multiple profiles are required — but the shape is NOT the one the audit assumed. The audit expected "several underlying-specific profiles pre-2026, collapsing to one 24/7 profile afterwards." That is wrong. The correct shape is SIX profiles before 2026-05-29 and SEVEN after, because only ECBTC went 24/7 and the other ten roots never collapsed into anything.

PROFILE COUNT AND MEMBERSHIP
  P1  ECES, ECNQ, ECRTY, ECYM   T=15:00:00   (ECBTC also a member 2023-03-12 .. 2026-05-28)
  P2  EC6E                       T=14:00:00
  P3  ECCL, ECNG                 T=13:30:00
  P4  ECGC                       T=12:30:00
  P5  ECSI                       T=12:25:00
  P6  ECHG                       T=12:00:00
  P7  ECBTC                      near-24/7, from 2026-05-29 only

WHY THESE CANNOT BE COLLAPSED INTO ONE ANOTHER
The six legacy profiles differ ONLY in the daily termination time T, but they differ in it by as much as three hours (12:00 vs 15:00). Every other element — the Sunday 16:00-17:00 pre-open, the Monday-Thursday 16:45-17:00 pre-open, the 17:00 open, the no-Friday-evening-reopen, the weekend close — is shared verbatim across all of them ("All Contracts: CME Globex Pre Open: Sunday 4:00 - 5:00 p.m. Monday - Thursday 4:45 - 5:00 p.m."). So they are six genuine profiles, not six coincidentally-similar ones; if the crate models a per-profile daily close, six keys are unavoidable. P5 (ECSI, 12:25:00) is the strongest argument against any merging heuristic: it sits five minutes from P4 (ECGC, 12:30:00), so any tolerance-based collapse would silently corrupt one of them.

WHY THEY CANNOT REUSE THE UNDERLYING FUTURES' PROFILES (the tempting wrong answer)
The audit's phrasing — "ECCL followed crude, ECGC followed gold" — invites reusing the crude/gold/equity-index keys. Do not. The event contract tracks the underlying's daily SETTLEMENT time, not the underlying's Globex close, and those are different instants. CME's own wording is the proof: "Daily products: trading will terminate at the end of the daily settlement period of the Underlying Futures contract." A settlement window ends hours before the underlying's Globex session does; ECES stops at 15:00 and stays dark until 17:00, whereas ES itself keeps trading past 15:00. The event contracts therefore need their OWN keys, semantically anchored to settlement times, even though the numbers were derived from the underlying complexes. (I did not re-verify the underlying futures' grids in this session — that assertion rests on the CME termination-of-trading language, not on a fresh reading of the ES/GC/CL specs.)

WHY P7 MUST BE ITS OWN KEY AND MUST NOT BE REUSED FROM CRYPTO
ECBTC's post-2026 grid is superficially "24/7 like the crypto complex" and the notices explicitly say the technology and timeline align with the cryptocurrency migration. Resist reusing a crypto key on that basis. ECBTC's daily maintenance is 15:00:00-16:02:00 — it inherited the 15:00 close from its old equity-index-settlement group, not from crypto — and its Saturday extended window is 02:00-04:00. A crypto key derived from the Cryptocurrency Futures and Options 24/7 migration is a different document with different boundaries; I did not read it and cannot vouch that the numbers match. Semantically ECBTC is a Chapter 23 event contract whose close is a settlement-time artifact, so it deserves its own key regardless of envelope coincidence.

ON THE "DON'T JUSTIFY REUSE FROM A MATCHING CURRENT ENVELOPE" RULE
P1 and P2 currently differ, so no temptation arises there. But note the trap in the other direction: from 2023-03-12 to 2026-05-28 ECBTC's envelope was IDENTICAL to ECES/ECNQ/ECRTY/ECYM, and CME's own specification page listed them on one line ("ECES; ECNQ; ECRTY; ECYM; ECBTC | Sunday 5:00 p.m. - Friday 3:00 p.m."). A crate that assigned ECBTC the P1 key on that evidence would have been silently wrong from 2026-05-29 onward. ECBTC's underlying is Bitcoin futures, a product family CME was always going to move to weekend trading; that product-family semantics, not the matching envelope, is what should have driven the key. Give ECBTC its own key across its whole history (2023-03-12 onward), with a revision at 2026-05-29 — do not alias it to P1 for the first three years and then fork it.

HISTORY FLOOR
Not engaged. The family's first sourced listing is 2022-09-18, well above the crate's January-2010 floor, so no floor-clamping question arises. ECBTC's own history must begin 2023-03-12, the first date a primary source lists that product.

result.reuse_verdict:
NEEDS ITS OWN KEY. One key for all eight roots — do not split equity-index from crypto.

Why it cannot reuse `globex_equity_index`:
- That key carries a `regular` RTH of 08:30-15:15 CT (src/calendar/schedules/futures/us/cme_group.rs, CME_REGULAR). SQF has no published RTH at all. Pointing QSPX/QNDX/QDOW/QRTY at that key would assert an RTH split that no CME document states for these contracts.
- That key's timeline runs from the January-2010 floor with dated revisions at 2012-11-18, 2015-09-20 and 2021-06-27 (removal of the 15:15-15:30 halt), plus the disputed Sunday-queue bracket. SQF did not exist before 2025-06-30, so every one of those revisions is inapplicable and reuse would silently back-date the family by fifteen years — a direct violation of "a family's history may begin only at the first source that LISTS that family's product."
- The fact that ES and QSPX currently return an identical open/close/preopen envelope from CME's trading-hours service is exactly the "matching current envelope" the brief says must not drive the verdict.

Why it cannot reuse `globex_cryptocurrency`:
- That key moved to 24/7 effective 2026-05-29 (CME submission 26-114). CME excluded SQF from that migration by name and by instrument table. QBTC/QETH/QSOL/QXRP are still on the five-day 17:00-16:00 CT grid today, verified product-by-product against CME's own trading-hours service on 2026-09-05. Reuse would produce a market that is open all weekend when it is in fact closed from Friday 16:00 CT.

Why the equity-index and crypto SQF roots share ONE key rather than two:
- Product-family semantics, not envelope coincidence. All eight are the same instrument type in the same rulebook chapter (CME 24 / CBOT 24), created by the same product design (Spot Equivalent Quoted Price + Financing Adjustment), and CME administers them as one family: SER-9506R prints ONE identical "Trading and Clearing Hours" cell in both its equity-index exhibit and its cryptocurrency exhibit; SER-9630RR reprints that same cell for QSOL/QXRP; SER-9739 amends "the Listing Schedule of all CME and CBOT Spot-Quoted Futures" in a single table spanning all eight. There is no document in which the equity SQF grid and the crypto SQF grid differ.
- The one thing that did threaten to split them — the 2026-05-29 crypto 24/7 migration — is precisely the event CME used to keep them together: it moved the crypto family away from SQF, not the crypto SQF away from the equity SQF.
- The distinct Globex security groups (D1/D2/D3/D4 equity, D5/D6/D7/D9 crypto) are a market-data partition on MDP channel 326 / market segment 74, not a schedule difference; all eight returned identical schedules.

Launch-date handling (the one wrinkle):
- The key's history begins 2025-06-30 for QSPX, QNDX, QRTY, QDOW, QBTC, QETH. QSOL and QXRP begin 2025-12-15. That is a per-root listing date, not a family clock revision — the grid is byte-identical. Model it the way cryptocurrency.rs already models ETH/MBT/MET joining a live family in 2021 ("their individual launch dates are intentionally not family-clock revisions"), i.e. one key from 2025-06-30 with QSOL/QXRP gated by their own listing date if the crate exposes per-root listing, and closed before it otherwise. The crate's January-2010 floor is far below both dates and is not engaged.

NEEDS ITS OWN KEY. Suggested: MarketHoursKey::GlobexWeather => "globex_weather", backed by a new schedules/futures/us/weather.rs.

The trap here is exactly the one the brief warns about: weather's CURRENT envelope is byte-identical to the existing GlobexEnergy (energy_metals) profile — extended SUN+MON_THU 17:00->16:00, order_entry SUN 16:00-17:00 plus MON_THU 16:45-17:00, regular empty, daily and weekend close true. Matching the current row is NOT a reason to reuse, and here it would be actively wrong:

1. HISTORY DIVERGES FOR FIFTEEN OF THE SIXTEEN IN-SCOPE YEARS. Weather closed at 15:15 CT from the January-2010 floor until 2025-04-13. Over that same span GlobexEnergy closed at 16:15 CT (2010 floor) and then 16:00 CT from Monday 2015-09-21. So for 2010-01 .. 2025-04-13 — about 92% of the audited timeline — reusing GlobexEnergy would report weather's daily close 60 to 75 minutes late every single day, and would fabricate a 2015 cutover weather never had. The 2015-09-04 and 2016-12-01 captures of CME's weather specification both still read 3:15 p.m., which is direct primary evidence that weather sat out the NYMEX/COMEX 2015 move. The two grids only converged on 2025-04-13, and by coincidence of arithmetic, not by a shared notice: SER-9519 names only weather.

2. PRODUCT-FAMILY SEMANTICS ARE DISJOINT. GlobexEnergy is documented as NYMEX CL/NG/HO/RB/BZ/PL/PA plus COMEX GC/SI/HG — physically-settled energy and metals on two different DCMs. Weather is CME (XCME), financially settled off a published temperature index, with its own Globex security group (HW futures / W7 options), its own rulebook chapters (CME 403/403A, 405/405A), its own Daily Bulletin section (24), and its own hours-notice channel. CME has never announced a weather hours change inside an energy/metals notice or vice versa; SER-9519 addresses "all weather futures and options" and nothing else. Folding weather into globex_energy would also mean a future CME notice touching only one of the two families could not be encoded without splitting the key anyway — a breaking persisted-wire change, since key names are the serde wire format.

3. NO OTHER EXISTING KEY IS CLOSE. globex_equity_index, globex_grains, globex_fx, globex_interest_rates, globex_livestock and globex_cryptocurrency all publish different grids; livestock is a same-day RTH family with an empty extended, the polar opposite shape.

result.reuse_verdict:
NEEDS ITS OWN KEY. Do not reuse globex_grains, and do not be fooled by the fact that the two envelopes are identical today.

The trap: as of 2022-10-02 the mini grid and the standard grain grid are byte-identical - 19:00-07:45 overnight, 08:30-13:20 day, same four queues. A reviewer looking only at a current envelope would conclude the key is redundant. It is not.

The product-family semantics are the opposite of redundant. CME built the mini contracts with a deliberate, permanent 30-minute-later close so that traders could offset mini against standard positions AFTER the standard settlement. CME says this in its own words twice: CFTC filing CBOT 13-092 footnote 1, "To maintain the traditional mini- to full-sized trading hours, both electronic and floor hours for CBOT Mini-Sized Corn, Soybean, and Wheat futures will close daily at 1:45 p.m. CT"; and SER-7044, "because mini-sized products have slightly longer trading hours and because mini- and standard-sized products allow for offsets, the mini-sized products continue to be a popular tool for adjusting positions at the end of each trading day for all categories of traders." That is a design property of the family, not an accident of one envelope.

The history bears it out. Over the roughly sixteen years from the January-2010 floor to today, the mini grid differs from the standard grain grid for about twelve of them:
  2010-01-01 .. 2012-05-19  DIFFERS  day close 13:45 vs 13:15; and from 2010-04-19 the PCP starts 13:45:30 vs 13:15:30
  2012-05-20 .. 2012-09-15  IDENTICAL  both 17:00-14:00 (the only overlap window before 2022)
  2012-09-16 .. 2013-04-06  DIFFERS  17:00-14:30 vs 17:00-14:00; PCP 14:40 vs 14:30
  2013-04-07 .. 2015-07-04  DIFFERS  08:30-13:45 vs 08:30-13:15
  2015-07-05 .. 2022-10-01  DIFFERS  08:30-13:45 vs 08:30-13:20 (the minis skipped SER-7395R entirely)
  2022-10-02 .. today       IDENTICAL
A caller asking for 2016, 2019 or 2021 through globex_grains would get a close 25 minutes too early on every trading day. That is precisely the failure the crate's existing grains comment - "Mini-sized Corn, Soybean, and Wheat diverged on 2012-09-16 and are not represented by this key" - was written to prevent, and the research shows the divergence is in fact older and longer than that comment implies: it predates the January-2010 floor and it survived until October 2022.

Two consequences for the model that follow from the same reasoning. First, the revision list is NOT a copy of the grains list: the minis have a 2012-09-16 revision the standard grains do not, they have NO 2015-07-05 revision, and they have a 2022-10-02 revision the standard grains do not. Second, MKC must live on this key and not on any KC-wheat key: on identically dated 2015 captures MKC closes 13:45 while KE closes 13:20. The KC lineage is a naming fact; the hours follow the mini design.

SER-6617 (referenced in the task for the 2013 change) COULD NOT BE RETRIEVED — 404 at every CME path and absent from the Wayback Machine. The 2013 cutover is instead sourced from two independent CME primaries that are at least as strong: CME Globex Notice #20130401 and CBOT Submission 13-092. The SER announcing the 2018 change likewise could not be identified by number: CME's notice index carries no descriptive titles for 2018-era SERs, so I sourced 2018 from CBOT Submission 18-001 and CME Globex Notice #20180115 instead.

The task's premise of a '2012-05-20 expansion' is CONFIRMED as the go-live date, but note the paper trail is not clean: CBOT Submission 12-144 (2012-05-16) certified the same grid for 'June 3, 2012, for trade date June 4, 2012'. No superseding filing appears in CME's 2012 index. The May 20/21 date rests on CME Globex Notice #20120518 (prospective) and CBOT Submission 12-188 (retrospective), which agree with each other. CME's AC-268 fact card captured 2012-05-26 still showed the OLD hours, i.e. that marketing PDF lagged the change by days — it does not contradict the notice.

cmegroup.com serves HTTP 403 to curl and other non-browser clients, and the Wayback 'save' endpoint is refused for CME HTML (HTTP 520) though it works for CME PDFs. All live-page quotes above were read by rendering the pages in a real browser. Every citation is publicly reachable without authentication; where a contemporaneous Wayback capture exists I have given it alongside the live URL. The modern CME contract-spec pages render their specs table from a client-side API that the Wayback Machine never captured, so archived spec pages from 2015 onward show 'There is currently no contract specs data for this product' and CANNOT be used to bracket changes — this is why the CFTC rule-filing indexes were the decisive route.
result.reuse_verdict:
ZR NEEDS ITS OWN KEY. It must not reuse the standard CBOT grains key.

Why, from product-family semantics and history rather than from a coincidentally matching envelope:

1. The divergence is a deliberate, product-specific exchange action, not an artifact. CBOT filed a standalone CFTC certification for Rough Rice ALONE (Submission 18-001, "Reduction of the Extended Trading Hours for Rough Rice Futures and Options Contracts"), on the basis of a rough-rice-industry survey, to concentrate liquidity in a thin market. Nothing about it is shared with corn/wheat/soy/oats. A key that lumps ZR with the grains would be asserting a relationship the exchange explicitly severed.

2. The divergence is live and current, and it is structural, not a five-minute edge case. Read the same day (2026-09-05) from CME's own spec pages: ZR extended = Sun-Thu 19:00-21:00 CT; Oats and Corn extended = Sun-Fri 19:00-07:45 CT. ZR's evening leg is 2 hours where the grains' is 12h45m. ZR has NO midnight-wrapping session at all since 2018-01-22, whereas every other CBOT grain does — that is a different session topology, not a different boundary. A caller resolving "is ZR open at 02:00 CT" gets the wrong answer on every single overnight for eight years and counting.

3. Nothing suggests re-convergence. CME's annual CFTC rule-filing indexes for 2018-2026 contain exactly one Rough Rice hours filing (the 2018 one) and no grain/oilseed hours filing that would restore ZR. The only other Rough Rice filings in that period are a market-maker program (2021, 21-458), price-limit rules (2023, 23-083) and annual milling-yield schedules — none touch hours.

4. HOWEVER — the history is genuinely shared up to the divergence, and the crate should model it that way rather than duplicating a parallel timeline by hand. From the January-2010 floor through 2018-01-21, ZR tracked the standard CBOT grain/oilseed grid EXACTLY through all three reorganisations, and CME named Rough Rice in each source document: the 2012-05-20 expansion to 17:00-14:00 CT, the 2013-04-07 split into 19:00-07:45 + 08:30-13:15, and the 2015-07-05 move of the RTH close to 13:20. There is no ZR-specific deviation anywhere in that span. So the correct shape is a ZR key whose revision list is identical to the grains key through 2015-07-05 and then adds one further revision at 2018-01-21 that the grains key does not have.

5. Do NOT key ZR together with the four mini-sized CBOT ag futures (XC, XW, XK, MKC) either. Those were separately truncated and then RE-ALIGNED to the standard grains grid effective 2022-10-03 (SER-9049), so they are on the grains envelope today and would drag ZR back to the wrong overnight.

One caveat that bears on key design: ZR is currently the only CBOT grain with this envelope, so any "shared key" for it would have exactly one member. If the crate's convention is to name keys after the venue-plus-product-family rather than after the shape, a dedicated ZR key (e.g. CBOT rough rice) is the honest encoding.
